subject: Ordering bars in bar charts with 2 layers in ggplot2 0.9?

messages.author: 2b26ba80ca7c05b8
messages.subject: Ordering bars in bar charts with 2 layers in ggplot2 0.9?
parts:
Hello,

Sorry this might be a beginner's question :-)
In version 0.8 van ggplot2, I could easily order the bars depending on
the value of the y variable. I installed version 0.9 and i can't get
the bars ordered anymore.

Here is an example dataset: 10 different sites (x) with quantitative
measurements including negative values (y)

MyData <- data.frame(
measurement = runif(10, min=-1, max=1),
site = gl(10, 1, 10, labels = letters[1:10])
)

This used to order the bars depending on the value of the measurement
variable (ggplot2 version 0.8):

MyData <- MyData[order(MyData$measurement),]
ggplot(MyData, aes(site)) +
geom_bar(subset = .(measurement <0),aes(y = measurement), stat =
"identity")+
geom_bar(subset = .(measurement >=0), aes(y = measurement), stat =
"identity")

I tried this:
MyData <- transform( MyData,site = reorder(site, rank(measurement)))
and it does the job without subsetting, but does not work with the
subsets...

Any suggestion?
Many thanks in advance!

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Ordering bars in bar charts with 2 layers in ggplot2 0.9?
parts:
For me it looks the same in ggplot2 0.8.9 and 0.9.0 -- they bars are in order without subset, but they're out of order with subset. My guess is that this is happening because ggplot is dropping the unused factor levels from each subset, then, when it puts the subsets back together, it recomputes the factor levels naively, so they get sorted alphabetically.

For me, using scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) fixes the problem. 


set.seed(124)

site        = letters[1:10]
)

# Order the levels of site, by values of measurement
MyData$site <- reorder(MyData$site, MyData$measurement)

# Bars in order
ggplot(MyData, aes(site, y=measurement)) + geom_bar()

# Bars not in order (with subset)
ggplot(MyData, aes(site, y=measurement)) +
  geom_bar(subset = .(measurement < 0)) +
  geom_bar(subset = .(measurement >= 0))

# Bars in order
ggplot(MyData, aes(site, y=measurement)) +
  geom_bar(data = subset(MyData, measurement < 0)) +
  geom_bar(data = subset(MyData, measurement >= 0)) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE)

-Winston

Thanks everyone for the suggestions! 

I know the 2 layers make no sense here, but I tried to show a short and reproducible example and the problem appears only with several layers, as some of you pointed.

 Problem solved, the drop=FALSE in the scale_x_discrete does the trick with several layers!

Cécile
